parsed.refutation_attempt: Attempted to determine whether the call to IsDefined(currentLink) on lines 32 and 38 provides a bounds check for nextLink1[currentLink] on lines 29 and 42. Since the implementation of IsDefined is not present in the fragment, it is unclear whether it verifies that currentLink is a valid index into nextLink1. No other explicit bounds checks or constant arguments are present, and the code paths to the sink are reachable. Without knowledge of IsDefined, the vulnerability cannot be conclusively confirmed or refuted.

finding.title: Out-of-bounds read
finding.assumptions: The input vectors (node1Data, node2Data, link1, nextLink1) are populated with user-controlled data or data that is not properly validated.

parsed.refutation_attempt: No neutralising checks were found. The code pushes values from node2Data into nodeStack without validating that those indices are within bounds of onStackFlag. The subsequent pop and access onStackFlag[w] at line 50 therefore has a clear path from untrusted input to an out‑of‑bounds read. No constant arguments, unreachable paths, or other safeguards mitigate this. The trigger condition w >= onStackFlag.size() is directly achievable with malicious node2Data values.

parsed.change_summary: Added a bounds check before accessing onStackFlag[w] in line 50.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger described in the finding no longer works because a bounds check has been added before accessing onStackFlag[w]. This ensures that w is within the valid range of the onStackFlag vector, preventing out-of-bounds reads.

parsed.notes: The patch adds a bounds check before accessing onStackFlag[w] and resSubData[w], effectively preventing the out-of-bounds read identified in the original code. The change is limited to the problematic line and does not alter other logic, preserving correct behavior for valid inputs. No new vulnerabilities are introduced by the patch.
